questions.question: How many surfaces does the lower end of the radius present?
questions.explanation: The lower end is the widest part of the bone and presents five surfaces.

questions.question: Which ligament attaches to the thick ridge on the anterior surface of the lower radius?
questions.explanation: The thick ridge on the anterior surface provides attachment to the palmar radio-carpal ligament of the wrist joint.

questions.question: Which surface of the lower radius contains the dorsal tubercle of Lister?
questions.explanation: The posterior surface presents the dorsal tubercle of Lister.

questions.question: Which structure is located immediately medial to the dorsal tubercle of Lister?
questions.explanation: The dorsal tubercle of Lister is located lateral to the groove for the tendon of extensor pollicis longus.

questions.question: Which tendons traverse the groove lateral to the Lister's tubercle?
options: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.explanation: The groove lateral to the Lister's tubercle is traversed by tendons of extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis.

questions.question: Which tendons pass through the groove medial to the groove for extensor pollicis longus?
options: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.explanation: Tendons of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis pass through this medial groove.

questions.question: Which structure is located on the medial surface of the lower end of the radius?
questions.explanation: The medial surface of the lower radius presents the ulnar notch for articulation with the head of ulna.

questions.question: What structure is attached to the lower margin of the ulnar notch?
questions.explanation: The articular disc of the inferior radio-ulnar joint is attached to the lower margin of the ulnar notch.

questions.question: Which muscle inserts at the base of the radial styloid process?
questions.explanation: The brachioradialis is inserted to the base of the styloid process.

questions.question: Which bone articulates with the medial quadrangular area of the inferior surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: The medial quadrangular area articulates with the lateral part of the lunate.

questions.question: Why are fractures of the radius more common than fractures of the ulna?
questions.explanation: The radius is a weight-bearing bone of the forearm, making it more prone to fractures.

questions.question: In a fracture of the radial shaft below the biceps insertion, the upper fragment is supinated by which muscle?
questions.explanation: The upper fragment in this specific fracture is supinated by the supinator muscle.

questions.question: In a fracture of the radial shaft, the lower fragment is pronated by which muscle?
questions.explanation: The lower fragment is pronated by the pronator teres.

questions.question: In a Colles' fracture, the distal fragment is displaced in which direction?
questions.explanation: In a Colles' fracture, the distal fragment is displaced backwards and upwards.

questions.question: Which fracture is described as the reverse of Colles' fracture?
questions.explanation: Smith's fracture is the reverse of Colles' fracture.

questions.question: A fracture of the styloid process of the radius is termed what?
questions.explanation: A fracture of the styloid process of the radius is termed a Chauffeur's fracture.

questions.question: The radius is most commonly fractured in which age group?
questions.explanation: The radius is the most commonly fractured bone in people over 50 years of age.

questions.question: What is the most common mechanism of injury for a radius fracture?
questions.explanation: It is often fractured as a result of a fall on an outstretched hand.

questions.question: How many ossification centers does the radius have?
questions.explanation: The radius ossifies from three centers: one primary and two secondary.

questions.question: During which week of intrauterine life does the primary ossification center appear?
questions.explanation: The primary center appears in the mid-shaft during the 8th week of intrauterine life.

questions.question: At what age does the center for the lower end of the radius appear?
questions.explanation: The center for the lower end appears at the age of the first year.

questions.question: During which year does the center for the upper end of the radius appear?
questions.explanation: The center for the upper end appears during the fifth year.

questions.question: At what age does the upper epiphysis of the radius fuse?
questions.explanation: The upper epiphysis fuses at the age of 12 years.

questions.question: At what age does the lower epiphysis of the radius fuse?
questions.explanation: The lower epiphysis fuses at the age of the 20th year.

questions.question: Madelung deformity is a congenital anomaly of which bone?
questions.explanation: Madelung deformity is a congenital anomaly of the radius.

questions.question: What causes the anterior bowing of the distal radius in Madelung deformity?
questions.explanation: The anterior bowing is due to an abnormal growth of the distal epiphysis.

questions.question: Between what ages does Madelung deformity typically occur?
questions.explanation: It occurs between 10 and 14 years of age.

questions.question: What happens to the distal epiphyseal line in Madelung deformity?
questions.explanation: There is premature disappearance of the distal epiphyseal line.

questions.question: Madelung deformity may cause subluxation or dislocation of which structure?
questions.explanation: There may be subluxation or dislocation of the distal end of the ulna.

questions.question: What is the underlying defect in Madelung deformity that affects the distal ulna?
questions.explanation: The subluxation of the ulna is due to defective development of the distal radial epiphysis.
